What is MarketMuse?

Content strategy platform that operates at the site and topic level rather than the page level - it models your entire site's topical authority, identifies gaps against competitors, and tells you what to write next and with what priority.

Best for

Site-wide content strategy and prioritisation, not single-page optimisation.

Main features

  • Personalised difficulty scoring based on your site's existing authority rather than a generic metric
  • topic modelling and inventory of your entire site
  • content gap analysis against named competitors
  • Topic Navigator building cluster plans
  • content briefs with structure and term guidance
  • Compete application analysing specific competitor pages
  • content inventory prioritising update, create or consolidate decisions
  • Optimize application for page-level work.

Practical use cases

  • Deciding which 50 articles to write next and in what order
  • identifying topical gaps that competitors cover and you do not
  • finding pages that should be consolidated rather than refreshed
  • building a defensible content roadmap for a year.

Who is it for?

  • Content strategists, enterprise SEO teams, publishers and agencies planning at portfolio scale.

Pricing, free access & limits

Subscription by queries/inventory size and seats; enterprise contracts

Plans described in the source

Free tier with roughly 10 queries per month. Optimize around $99/mo ($79 annually) with limited queries and 1 seat. Research around $249/mo ($199 annually) with more queries and applications. Strategy around $499/mo ($399 annually) with full inventory, Compete and multiple seats. Enterprise/Premium custom, annual - historically in the four to five figures per month for large sites. Annual billing roughly 20% cheaper.

Free plan

Yes - a free tier with roughly 10 queries per month, enough to evaluate the model.

Free trial

Free tier serves as the trial; enterprise pilots via sales.

Usage limits to consider

Metered by queries (topic analyses) per month. Site inventory size, competitor tracking and seat counts are tier-limited. Full inventory analysis of a large site consumes substantial allowance.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Personalised difficulty scored against your own site's authority is genuinely better than generic keyword-difficulty metrics - it answers 'can we rank for this' rather than 'is this hard in general'
  • site-wide inventory with create/update/consolidate recommendations is strategic advice no page-level tool provides
  • the free tier lets you test the core model properly.

Limitations to consider

  • Expensive, with the genuinely useful tiers starting around $249/mo
  • steep learning curve and the outputs require SEO expertise to interpret and act on
  • English-centric with poor multilingual support
  • query metering makes large-site analysis costly
  • overkill for anyone publishing fewer than a few articles a month
  • the product has been through ownership changes affecting roadmap confidence.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web
  • Google Docs add-on
  • WordPress plugin
  • API

Languages

  • Primarily English-optimised; other language support is limited and Arabic is not well served

API access

Yes - MarketMuse API available on higher tiers

Integrations and exports

  • Google Docs, WordPress, Google Search Console, Contentful, Zapier

Evaluation notes

MarketMuse answers a different question from Surfer or Clearscope - what to write versus how to write it - so they are complements, not alternatives. Use the free tier to test whether the personalised difficulty scores match your actual ranking experience before paying.
